name: Liverpool City Council

departments.name: Licensing and Regulatory Services
departments.notes: Handles Licensing Act 2003 (alcohol, entertainment, late night refreshment) and Gambling Act 2005 premises. Uses LALPAC system for online applications and register searches. Blue notice must be displayed at premises and notice published in local newspaper. Objection period is 28 days. Text Relay calls welcomed.

departments.name: Taxi and Private Hire Licensing
departments.notes: No longer accepts document submissions by email - documents will not be processed. All applications must be submitted through the online licensing portal. Twitter/X: @lcc_licensing for updates.

departments.name: Property Licensing (HMO)
departments.notes: HMO licensing mandatory for properties with 5+ persons forming 2+ households sharing amenities. Uses LAR (Licensing and Regulations) portal for applications and register searches. Must email privatesector.housing@liverpool.gov.uk to report any changes in licence holder circumstances. Flats in purpose-built blocks with 3+ self-contained units may not need HMO licence - contact to confirm.

departments.name: Selective Licensing
departments.notes: Selective Licensing Scheme runs from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2027. Covers 16 wards: Anfield, Central, County, Everton, Fazakerley, Greenbank, Kensington, Kirkdale, Old Swan, Picton, Princes Park, Riverside, St Michael's, Tuebrook & Stoneycroft, Warbreck, Wavertree. Covers approximately 80% of privately rented homes in Liverpool (45,000 of 55,000). Full licence fee: £550 per property (discounts available). Social housing and HMOs already licensed are exempt.

departments.name: Street Trading
departments.notes: Council not currently granting new licences. Three consent types available: Daily (up to 5 days), Long-term (up to 12 months), Football ground (match days at Anfield/Goodison Park). Daily consent: £66.24 initial + £20.14/day. Long-term static: £892.09 (grant), £348.69 (renewal). Non-refundable application fee: £70. Currently accepting applications for Waterloo Place only.

departments.name: Markets
departments.notes: For market stall applications, download paper form and return to Liverpool Food Hub. Market operators running temporary markets/events/festivals with 5+ stalls/retail units must apply for Market Rights Licence. Includes indoor markets, casual markets, and farmers markets.

departments.name: Planning
departments.notes: Applications submitted via national Planning Portal. Use planning@liverpool.gov.uk for help locating decision notices. For BACS payments: planningandbuildingcontrol@liverpool.gov.uk. Area-specific contacts: planning.dccitycentre@liverpool.gov.uk, planning.dcnorth@liverpool.gov.uk, planning.dcsouth@liverpool.gov.uk. Online contact speeds up process. Text Relay calls welcomed.

departments.name: Building Control
departments.notes: Building Control partner scheme available for frequent applicants. Handles building control reversion if private approved inspector cannot continue. Report dangerous buildings/structures through same contact. Text Relay calls welcomed. LABC member - part of Merseyside LABC partnership.

departments.name: Highways (Traffic Orders)
departments.notes: TTRO application requires confirmed start date with council and issued PAA number. Liverpool is Local Highway Authority for all public roads, footways and footpaths. If TTRO affects pay and display bays, must contact Parking Services for revenue reimbursement. Council can take action against unlicensed structures/activities on highway.

departments.name: Environmental Health
departments.notes: Investigates health and safety complaints about workplaces including reportable accidents, dangerous occurrences and diseases. Only investigates food safety matters presenting significant risk to public health (rats, mice, cockroaches, poor food handling). All food businesses must register with council. Also responsible authority for licensing consultations.

departments.name: Trading Standards
departments.notes: Handles trading and consumer advice. Also responsible authority for licensing consultations.

researchNotes: Research conducted via Liverpool City Council website and web searches. All council departments based at Cunard Building, Water Street. Uses LALPAC system for licensing applications and registers. Selective Licensing Scheme (2022-2027) covers 16 wards - approximately 80% of private rentals. Street trading licences currently restricted - not granting new licences, only accepting Waterloo Place applications. Taxi licensing no longer accepts email submissions - all applications via portal. Building Control part of Merseyside LABC partnership. Merseyside Police (Rose Hill, Cazneau Street) and Fire Service (Bootle HQ) are key responsible authorities. Main switchboard: 0151 233 3000. Planning/Building Control: 0151 233 3021. Licensing: 0151 233 3015. Highways: 0151 233 3001.
